title: Man. Post. Cap. VIII: proximate cause in us — why impute alien actual sin?
pass_a_gloss: Why hunt so far for the near cause of evils we all bear, when it stands next to you? Why look for it in Adam when each of us displays it? Why must God charge us with another's sin when he already finds in us a sin that earns those pains? Why charge an actual deed we never did in act or power, while he sees in each a vice now sticking in us and deserving those pains?
pass_b_english: Why do you seek so far the proximate cause of the evils which we all suffer, when it meets you near at hand? Why do you seek it in Adam when in each of us it shows itself? Why is it needful that God impute to us an alien sin, when in us he finds a sin which merits those penalties? Why should he impute an actual sin which we did neither in act nor in potency, when he sees in each of us a vice actually inhering, worthy of those penalties?
source_text: Cur tam longe quaeris causam proximam malorum quae omnes patimur, cum occurrat in proximo? Cur eam quaeris in Adamo cum in nobis singulis se prodat? Cur opus est ut Deus nobis imputet peccatum alienum, cum in nobis inveniat peccatum quod illas poenas meretur? Cur imputet actuale quod neque actu neque potentia fecimus, cum videat in singulis nobis vitium actu inhaerens dignum illis poenis?

choices.choice: Why seek far in Adam / impute alien when vice in us merits
